newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close down, further falls seen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close down, further falls seen.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates ended lower on Thursday on easing liquidity as the central bank halted its recent liquidity mop-up measures and an exodus of funds into the stock market showed signs of slowing.

As the liquidity squeeze eased, the overnight interbank rate settled to end at 7.048 percent against Wednesday's 7.274 close -- still outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but far below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper was at 7.00-7.25 percent against 7.25-7.50.
Many dealers saw room for the rates to fall further as the central bank appeared to have slightly softened its "not too loose" monetary policy.

The stock market on Thursday rebounded sharply from two previous sessions of profit-taking to close 2.68 percent higher, but turnover was relatively moderate at T$151 billion -- the lightest for a full session since June 13.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield rose in the face of the stock market's strong rebound. The 86/4 bond yield was traded at 5.9975 in late trade against Wednesday's 5.9775.
